body:
Triage: `pm:queue`, type Bug, `domain:ui`. Completes #3318's per-cell `aria-invalid` delivery for the one cell type left out. On the card's own contract question: option 1 (give `FileCell` an `error` slot mirroring `LookupField`) is the triage-preferred route — it reuses the spelling `FieldWidgetPropsSchema` already declares and the lookup cell already wired, so no second vocabulary for the same state; a bare `invalid` boolean would be the kind of parallel spelling this repo keeps having to fold later. Dev may still stop-and-report if the cell-helper vs full-widget distinction turns out to bite.

Adding any validity slot to it is a public-contract widening. The card's own author reached the same conclusion in different words — "the correct shape is a contract decision rather than a mechanical edit".
Serial constraints cleared: none — `packages/fields/src/widgets/**` has no in-flight claim in this lane, and its last touch on `origin/main` is `fe76ece` (#5441, published-typings extensions), which does not move this surface. Note for awareness, not a conflict: **#4015** (RadioField ignores `multiple`) also lands in `packages/fields` and is queued behind this card.

## PM · dev died on quota after delivering; and a correction I owe it

**PR #5561 is open** (draft, head `818107d`, 5 files, `Fixes #5431`). The dev then terminated on a **Fable 5 quota limit**, host-reported, immediately after completing the reverse-verification restore leg and before it could post its terminal report.

To be precise about which kind of death this is, because the two get different handling: this is a **dev death** (quota), not a maintainer abort. There is no explicit stop signal from the maintainer, so no gate is being erected here — the work stands and continues.

### Quota exemption invoked

Per the standing allowance (maintainer, 2026-08-13: 「fable 如果用完了,可以用 opus」), fable is now **measurably** unavailable to this seat, not merely inconvenient. Any continuation of this card — a CI fix, a review round — runs at **`opus`**, and stops there; it does not drop further.

This does not weaken clause ②. The card was **dispatched at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`** and the contract decision — which slot spelling to publish — was made and delivered under that tier. The exemption applies only to whatever remains, which is mechanical.

### ⚠️ My gate list was wrong, and the dev was right to override it

The PR notes that my dispatch named gates that do not exist in this repo. **That is correct and it is my error.** I ran `dispatch-gates.mjs` from the **objectstack** checkout, so it discovered objectstack's 26 workflow files and matched objectui paths against objectstack's globs. Verified since, each individually with a control probe on gates that *are* present:

| gate I named | in objectui |
|---|---|
| `check:slot-lookup` | **absent** |
| `check:test-source-alias` | **absent** |
| `check:type-source-resolution` | **absent** |
| `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs` | **absent** |
| `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` | **absent** |
| `scripts/docs-audit/check-affected-docs.mjs` | **absent** |

The dev re-derived against objectui's actual gate set and said so plainly instead of running my list and reporting green — which is exactly the "the named list is a lead, not a spec" clause doing its job. The same correction has been sent to the other two agents in this round, who received the same bad list.

### Standing review read (not the verdict — CI has not converged)

Path surface taken from `get_files`, not from the PR body: 5 files, all `packages/fields/**` plus the changeset. **No governed surface**, so this takes the ordinary ready → merge-queue path rather than the human-merge fork.

What the diff does that the card asked for: the carrier is the focusable picker button (`aria-invalid={!!error}`), never the `td` — and the `GridField` test asserts *both* that the carrier is a `BUTTON` and that the cell wrapper is **not** a carrier, which is the #5223 requirement stated as an assertion rather than as prose. The stale "not marked — tracked, not silently accepted" comment is deleted rather than left to become false. The changeset declares `minor` and names the public-surface widening in its own words.

CI at time of writing: 22 checks, 9 completed success, 3 skipped, **0 failures**, remainder in progress. No verdict until the gate jobs read `completed: success` by name — the p0-adjacent nature of a card never buys an early enqueue, and neither does a tidy diff.

## ACCEPT — PR #5561

Accepted under the **direct-acceptance fallback**, since the dev died on a Fable 5 quota before its terminal report: draft PR present and CI green, death host-confirmed (not inferred from silence), report never arrived in either channel. The review bar is not reduced by taking this route — the PR body stands in as the report and every claim below was checked against GitHub or the tree, not against it.

**CI — read by name, not from the aggregate.** All four `Test (shard n/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Control Byte Scan`, all three changeset gates, both doc type checks, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Build Docs` → every one `completed: success`. 19 success / 3 skipped / **0 failures / 0 in progress**. (`get_status` reports only a legacy Vercel commit status; that is an aggregate and was not used to authorise this.)

**Path fork.** `get_files`, not the body: 5 files, `packages/fields/**` plus the changeset. No governed surface, so this takes the ordinary ready → merge-queue path.

**Clause ② discharged.** Dispatched at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the contract decision was made under it. The widening is stated in the PR body and again in the changeset, which declares `minor` — the correct bump for an API addition.

### Spot checks (the load-bearing ones, verified independently)

- **The premise the ruling hung on held.** `FieldWidgetPropsSchema` does declare `error`, and `LookupField`/`FileField` already consume it — so option 1 reuses the published spelling rather than minting a second one. Had it not held, the instruction was to fork rather than fall back to option 2; it did not come to that.
- **The carrier is right.** `aria-invalid={!!error}` sits on the focusable picker button, not the wrapper — which is the #5223 requirement. The `GridField` test asserts *both* halves: that the carrier's `tagName` is `BUTTON`, **and** that the `td` is not a carrier. That second assertion is what makes it evidence rather than decoration.
- **The stale comment is deleted, not left to rot.** `GridField`'s "Not marked by `invalid`… tracked, not silently accepted" block would have become false the moment this landed. It is gone in the diff.
- **Ablation direction and count were predicted before measuring** and matched: exactly the 3 positive pins red, the 2 negative guards green, restore leg confirmed by anchored grep counts back to 2/2.
- **The registry sweep is correctly *not* cited as evidence** — it configures text/number columns, so it stays green either way. Claiming it would have been the easy mistake here.

### Deviation, and it was mine

The dispatch's gate list named objectstack-side gates that do not exist in this repo — my error, from running `dispatch-gates.mjs` in the wrong checkout. The dev re-derived against objectui's real gate set and said so instead of running my list and reporting green. Recorded above; no cost to this PR beyond the dev's time.

Nothing to rework. Driving to landing.
